name: Preposition Distribution Pattern
description: Analyzes the frequency and structural placement of prepositions (e.g., 'of', 'in', 'to', 'for', 'with'). Large Language Models tend to over-rely on prepositional phrases to connect generic clauses and maintain a steady, formal rhythm. This results in a statistically higher density of prepositions and highly predictable chaining (e.g., noun + 'of' + noun + 'in' + noun) compared to natural human writing, which uses more varied syntactic structures.
mechanism: The algorithm parses the text to isolate all prepositional elements. It then calculates three specific metrics: 1) Over-representation (measuring the raw percentage of prepositions against total word count, as AI often exceeds typical human thresholds), 2) Preposition Chaining (detecting consecutive prepositional phrases like 'in the pursuit of excellence in the field of science', a classic hallmark of AI 'filler' generation), and 3) Lexical Variety (AI tends to lean heavily on the top 10 most common prepositions, whereas human writers utilize a broader, more nuanced spatial/temporal vocabulary). By mapping these metrics against established linguistic baselines, the system flags texts that use prepositions as a mathematical 'glue' to string together otherwise hollow semantic blocks.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing student essays, corporate reports, and academic abstracts where AI is often employed to stretch word counts and mimic formal academic padding.
strengths:
• Targets a subconscious grammatical tic that prompters rarely think to modify or hide.
• Highly resilient against simple synonym replacement, as prepositions form the structural core of the sentence.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing genuine academic or legal writing, which naturally relies heavily on complex prepositional phrases for precision.
• Requires a sufficiently large text sample (typically >200 words) to establish a statistically significant distribution pattern.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tagging (Preposition Isolation) and Syntax Chaining
Metric: Depth of Prepositional Cascades and Overall Density
Output: 0-100 Prepositional Over-Reliance (Artificiality) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 70-80% accuracy. Best used as a supporting metric alongside lexical density and sentence length variance, rather than a standalone definitive test.

references.title: Bandi, A. et al. (2023). Lexical Features of AI-Generated vs Human-Written Text. IEEE.
Fröhling, L. & Zubiaga, A. (2021). Feature-based Detection of Automated Language Models. PeerJ Computer Science.
